function.name: search
function.description: Search the corpus with one or more queries simultaneously. The top matching documents (union across all queries) are added to your working directory; documents already there from earlier searches are kept (the working directory accumulates evidence across this session). Returns a per-query top-10 preview with file paths and short snippets, and the new total working-directory size. Pass multiple complementary queries in one call. Specific distinctive terms (rare phrases, proper nouns, distinctive number/date combinations) tend to give the best results.

function.name: bash
function.description: Run a bash command in the current working directory. Useful for searching with `rg`, `grep`, listing with `ls`, `find`, or reading with `cat`, `head`. Output is truncated; use focused patterns and flags like `-l` to keep results manageable.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in seconds; the backend clamps it to 1–60 seconds (default 60).

function.name: read
function.description: Read an imported original document. Offsets and limits are in LINES; offsets are zero-based. The default limit is 2000 lines when limit is omitted; this is a fallback, not a recommended read size. Set limit explicitly for each read. Prefer a rerank item's read_args or a located section's line range to inspect the needed original context directly. For an unfamiliar document without a located range, start with offset=0, limit=60 to inspect its header and any table of contents, then read the relevant body sections. If navigation or a long table of contents fills that preview, advance offset or increase limit explicitly; do not treat the preview as proof that evidence is absent. For additional body context, 100–200 lines is a starting point, not a cap: expand or page as needed, and use a larger explicit limit when a complete section or document is necessary. These rules also apply to short or single-topic documents. Line counts are not token budgets; this tool has no total token/byte output cap. Individual long lines may be truncated at 2000 characters. Character coordinates differ from these line arguments. If read_may_truncate is true, use the item's bash_args for exact passage recovery.

file_path.description: Path relative to the working directory.

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (0-indexed). Default 0.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read. Set this explicitly: start with 60 lines for an unfamiliar document, or use a known section's range or a rerank item's read_args. Expand or page when needed; 2000 is only the fallback if omitted.

function.name: rerank
function.description:
Find relevant original-body passages for your explicit evidence goal. Choose query, imported file subset, BM25 candidate count, retained count and output size yourself. Omitted files means the whole accumulated pool; [] means an empty scope. Returns source paths and read/bash coordinates, without restricting bash/read. For paging, supply result_id instead of query/file_paths/bm25_candidates; top_k, offset and limit can change without rescoring. Scores are relevance rankings, not verification of facts.

Optional file-subset example (the entity names and paths below are fictional placeholders):
1. To locate candidate files for an already identified entity, call bash with {"command": "rg -l -i 'EXAMPLE_ENTITY|EXAMPLE_ALIAS' ."}. Suppose it returns only these paths:
./docs/example_a.txt
./docs/example_b.txt
2. Explicitly pass those observed paths to rerank, for example: {"query": "EXAMPLE_ENTITY specific missing relationship", "file_paths": ["docs/example_a.txt", "docs/example_b.txt"], "bm25_candidates": 200, "top_k": 30, "limit": 5}. BM25 candidate selection and neural reranking then use only that file subset. The values 200/30/5 are adjustable examples, not required settings.
3. Inspect useful passages in their original context by passing an item's actual returned read_args to read. For example, if read_args is {"file_path": "docs/example_a.txt", "offset": 40, "limit": 12}, call read with that object; use the returned coordinates rather than copying the example coordinates.
You decide whether this sequence is useful; it is not required for every question. Do not automatically treat the preceding bash output as the rerank scope: it may contain body text, errors or truncated output. Check the returned paths and explicitly set file_paths yourself. Omitting file_paths still ranks the full accumulated pool. Selecting a subset affects only that rerank call; bash/read retain access to the full original-document pool.

query.description: Explicit fact or relationship to verify, including known entity names; required for a new ranking.

file_paths.description: Optional list of already imported relative source paths, such as files selected with bash; omitted or null means the accumulated pool.

bm25_candidates.description: M: number of scope-local BM25 passages sent to the neural reranker; default 1000, adjustable per call.

top_k.description: K: retain up to this many ranked passages; K <= M. Default min(100,M), or the first request's K on a result page.

offset.description: Zero-based offset into the retained ranking; default 0.

limit.description: Number of complete passages to return on this page; default 10, adjustable per call.

result_id.description: Tool-returned current ranking ID for pagination; mutually exclusive with query/file_paths/bm25_candidates.
